efficient cost structure and to hold credit cost below 1%. 
This consistency is the foundation on which we have built this business over the past 2 years. 
Against these priorities, the quarter has progressed well. Our total disbursements grew 28% Y-

INR11,917 crores. Our doorstep gold loan offering maintained its momentum with AUM

We have opened 74 branches this quarter, taking our total gold branch count to 831. We expect

India, expanding our geographical footprint into newer and promising markets. The revised gold 
lending LTV framework continues to work its way through the system. Our gold GNPA at 0.5%

progress this quarter with disbursements growing 12% Y-o-Y to INR855 crores and the AUM 
grew 13.5% Y-o-Y to INR9,982 crores. Our focus remains on disciplined underwriting and 
portfolio quality. 
Within mortgage, our medium ticket LAP disbursed INR645 crores, reflecting 16% Y-o-Y 
increase while maintaining the yields at stable levels. Our small ticket LAP and housing business 
disbursed INR210 crores as our investment in credit policy leadership and BRE-driven 
underwriting engine begins to translate into lower credit cost. Our on-book portfolio remains 
fully secured with the unsecured loans constituting less than 1% of our on-book assets. 
Turning to profitability and asset quality. Credit costs for the quarter came in at INR27 crores, 
approximately 0.6% of the average total assets as on an annualized basis, continuing to track 
well within our guided range of - below 1%. The quarter concluded with a profit after tax of 
INR130.8 crores, a Y-o-Y growth of 63% and ROA of 2.8% and an ROE of 17%. 
On the asset quality, our GNPA stood at 1.8%, moving from 1.6% in Q1. The movement is 
primarily attributable to the ongoing transition in gold loan lending practices and the flattish as 
we did our direct assignment and co-lending business normalized in the quarter. NNPA stands 
at 1.2%, with a provision coverage ratio at 35.4%. On a Y-o-Y basis, both the GNPA and NNPA 
have improved, the capital adequacy stands at 21%, and book value per share stands at 84.4. 
Taken together, the quarter reflects a business that is growing well with improving asset quality, 
resilient core earnings, our highest ever ROE at 17%, the foundation we have built over the past 
2 years, a fully secured book, a scaled gold loan franchise, a stabilized mortgage business and a 
strengthened collection organization is now in place, and we believe it positions us well for the 
quarters ahead.

detail

In spite of the turbulent headwinds over this quarter and lack of momentum in gold prices, we 
continue on our theme of building resilience across business cycles. Quarter 2 '27 has been our 
strongest quarter to date in terms of profitability and operating metrics. 
Over the last 8 quarters, we have been on the journey of building a business model which results 
in consistent noncyclical and predictable earnings. The linear upward trajectory of ROA and 
ROE expansion over the last 8 to 9 quarters is the validation of the resilience in that model. We 
shared last quarter that we had crossed the interim ROE milestone of 15%. 
I will reiterate four headline numbers that summarize our performance for quarter 2. The first 
one is on the ROA. The ROA expanded sequentially quarter-on-quarter by 24 bps to 2.8%. The 
last 9 quarters have seen ROA slowly but steadily inching up from 2.1% to 2.8%. The ROE 
expansion sequentially has been 153 bps quarter-on-quarter to 17% in Q2. This also represents 
a steady increase from 10.9% ROE to 17% ROE over the last 9 quarters. We remain optimistic 
on continuing on this trajectory. We started the fiscal with an AUM of a little over INR20,000 
crores. We crossed the milestone of INR22,000 crores in September, representing a 9% increase 
in the first half of the year. 
The credit cost shrunk by 18 bps from 0.78% to 0.6% of total assets, as the flows from the 
mortgage book have materially improved in aiding and lowering credit costs. Our growing ROE 
enhances our ability to fund the loan book expansion through internal accruals and puts us on an 
accelerating journey of book value compounding. 
Let me now walk you through a little more detail on the numbers.  
First, on the P&L items. Core NII grew 5.2% quarter-on-quarter to INR404.8 crores and 40.9% 
year-on-year. Pre-operating profit of INR205.1 crores is up 9.4% sequentially quarter-on-quarter 
and 47.5% year-on-year. 
Our credit costs declined to INR27.1 crore in quarter 2, down 20.5% quarter-on-quarter from 
INR34.1 crore in quarter 1 due to improving collection efficiencies on the mortgage book. 
Consequently, the PAT came in at INR130.8 crores, up 14.3% quarter-on-quarter and 
approximately 63.1% year-on-year. 
Now on yields and the cost of borrowing. Our overall yield on the core loan book remained 
constant in quarter 2 compared to quarter 1 at 16.40 levels. The optical increase in yield by 29 
bps is because the last quarter had a higher DA unwinding impact of around the same magnitude. 
On the cost of borrowing, in spite of headwinds, we were able to keep our weighted average cost 
of borrowing for quarter 2, flat at the same level as the previous 3 quarters at 7.80. This is 
represented in the funding profile slide in the deck. Our fixed rate borrowings form 33% of the 
book. This, coupled with the MCLR-linked loans, which constitute another 24% of our 
borrowing and have had a lesser magnitude of transmission historically, gives us some insulation 
against headwinds of increasing interest rates. We did direct assignments of approximately 
INR700 crores of the gold loan book to deleverage. This aided by higher co-lending in the gold 
portfolio, helped in bringing down the debt-equity ratio from 4.9% to 4.6% and improved capital 
adequacy to 21%, up from 20.7% in quarter 1.

Now on asset quality. Our mortgage delinquency numbers across stages are flat to better than 
the previous quarter. On the gold side, we had guided in quarter 1 that the shift to the periodic 
interest due model instead of the earlier bullet loan model was likely to result in technical 
delinquencies across stages going up as customer behaviour may take some more time to adjust. 
The increase in Stage II from 2.7% to 3.6% and in Stage III from 1.6% to 1.8% are entirely on 
account of this changed construct in gold loans. We are sufficiently collateralized and do not see 
these optical indicators as indicating any enhanced risk on the portfolio. 
We have had a record low level of net slippages in the mortgage book. It has been our best 
quarter till date. The decrease in PCR from 38.4% to 35.5% is due to a higher proportion of gold 
loans in Stage III. These gold loans carry a much lesser provisioning coverage per ECL. Our 
mortgage PCR continues at similar levels. 
Now on the operating leverage. Opex as a percentage of average total assets in the ROA tree 
stood at 4.9% in quarter 2 compared to 4.8% in quarter 1, reflecting the full quarter impact of 
the branch and headcount additions. This is materially down from 5.5% in FY26 and the 
structural reduction in cost intensity over the medium term remains intact. Our cost to income 
came in at 52.5% in quarter 2, marginally better than the 52.8% in quarter 1. For context, the 
annualized cost to income in FY26 was 57.2%. The step-up in operating expenses this quarter is 
primarily driven by the branch expansion program. 
In addition to the 74 branches we added in quarter 2, we propose to add at least another 150 
branches in the second half of the year. While this will add to the investment Opex, we are 
hopeful of containing any material increases in cost to income over current levels by focused 
effort on our BAU Opex. 
To summarize, our expanding ROAs and ROEs and our focus on the productivity and operating 
leverage levers provide us with shock buffers to potential headwinds on the interest rates or any 
insurance distribution related changes. We remain deeply grateful for the continued support of 
our investors, both old and new, and all of you on this call who have been with us thus far on 
this journey. 
With that, I now hand it over to the floor for Q&A.
